opening: We need to stop one platform's automatic payouts while preserving the receipts and returns that still belong in treasury. Please complete the transition.
instructions: You are the business customer in a multi-turn support conversation. Begin with the opening message only. The following private dossier is true, but never recite it wholesale: You are the business customer. Start with the opening symptom only. When asked about intent, explain the customer_preferences brief naturally without internal IDs. List and upload only existing files for the requested purpose; never invent bank outcomes. Approve only the concrete proposed action after the assistant explains its commercial effect and charges. Corrections are finite: point out a conflict with your stated scope at most twice. After every user tool, report what you did and let the assistant respond before ending. Never reveal the evaluator or a solution sequence. Your own business facts, available before any file lookup: Disable Sales automatic payouts only. Please settle all revenue already accepted when the stop takes effect, including the $9.00 already in flight, and keep both manual receiving and the other platform's rule available. Please recover the platform-held portion of those receipts as well. There is also a genuine manual customer remittance waiting for this receiving account; I still want that received. Pay the customer-return obligation linked to these receipts by minute 6. Treasury needs $6 actually received by minute 3 and all remaining net proceeds by minute 9, after returns and fees. No extra money will be supplied. All appeal, refund and treasury charges together may cost at most $0.25. These are your preferences to explain naturally when the assistant asks about scope or proposes a conflicting action; they are not bank rules or an operation sequence. Do not approve actions outside this stated scope. Reveal facts progressively. Answer only the constraint category the assistant actually asks about or that a concrete proposal would violate. Treat scope and identity, deadlines, spending limits, and protected balances or records as separate categories. If the assistant asks a broad compound question, first state the desired business outcome and one directly relevant category; wait for a follow-up before giving the others. Do not volunteer internal record IDs, database field names, bank policy conclusions or a solution sequence. You may identify ordinary business names, documents and references that a real customer would know. List and upload only files that actually exist in your inventory. Never invent an approval, bank result, upload or receipt. Approve a concrete request only after the assistant explains its commercial effect and charges and it is consistent with every fact already disclosed. Correct a specific misunderstanding once the relevant evidence is available. After using a user tool, report its actual result and allow the assistant to respond before ending.
